title: Fourfold Displays for 'ggplot2'
text: fourfold display special case radial diagram, “polar area chart”, designed \(2 \times 2\) (\(2 \times 2 \times k\)) tables (Fienberg, 1975; Friendly, 1994a, 1994b). frequency \(n_{ij}\) cell shown quarter circle whose radius proportional \(\sqrt{n_{ij}}\), area proportional cell count. Like pie chart, uses segments circle show frequencies; unlike pie chart, keeps angles segments constant varies radius. main purpose display show sample odds ratio, \[ \hat{\theta} = \frac{n_{11} / n_{12}}{n_{21} / n_{22}}              = \frac{n_{11} \, n_{22}}{n_{12} \, n_{21}} . \] association two variables (\(\theta \neq 1\)) appears tendency one pair diagonally opposite cells larger pair. Color diagonal tick marks show direction association: relatively larger diagonal pair drawn blue (expected independence) tick marks along diagonal, pair red. Confidence rings around quadrant give visual test independence, \(H_0: \theta = 1\): standardized display, rings adjacent quadrants overlap observed counts consistent null hypothesis.

title: Fourfold Displays for 'ggplot2'
text: classic example, UCBAdmissions gives applicants six largest graduate departments Berkeley 1973, classified admission gender (Bickel et al., 1975). geom_fourfold() currently works data long form: map two-level variables x (drawn left right) y (drawn top bottom), cell frequencies weight. Without faceting, rows cell summed, pools departments: unstandardized display (std = "ind.max") shows raw frequencies, largest cell drawn full size. sample odds ratio, Odds(Admit | Male) / Odds(Admit | Female), \((1198 / 1493) / (557 / 1278) = 1.84\): male applicants nearly twice likely admitted.  comparisons difficult male applicants female, applicants rejected admitted. unstandardized display confidence rings interpretation test \(H_0: \theta = 1\). data can standardized make comparison easier preserving odds ratio. margin = 1 rows (, Gender) equated, quadrant shows proportion men women admitted rejected: 44.5% male applicants admitted, compared 30.4% female applicants. Now rings upper quadrant overlap quadrant odds ratio differ 1.  default, margin = c(1, 2), standardizes margins. four quadrants align horizontally vertically odds ratio 1, regardless marginal frequencies, association admission gender can seen without influence overall admission rate numbers men women applied. fully standardized display usually useful form.  quadrants align, 95% confidence rings, computed interval \(1.62 \le \theta \le 2.09\), overlap: odds ratio differs significantly 1, apparent evidence gender bias favour men.
code: ucb <- as.data.frame(UCBAdmissions) berkeley <- ggplot(ucb, aes(x = Admit, y = Gender, weight = Freq)) +   theme_fourfold() berkeley + geom_fourfold(std = "ind.max") berkeley + geom_fourfold(margin = 1) berkeley + geom_fourfold()

title: Fourfold Displays for 'ggplot2'
text: quadrant fourfold display drawn pair thin rings, one just inside one just outside edge. Together show range tables consistent data confidence level given conf_level (0.95 default). constructed three steps. 1. interval odds ratio. Inference simplest log scale. log odds ratio, \(\hat{\psi} = \log \hat{\theta}\), approximate standard error \[ \hat{s}(\hat{\psi}) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n_{11}} + \frac{1}{n_{12}} +                             \frac{1}{n_{21}} + \frac{1}{n_{22}}} , \] approximate \(1 - \alpha\) confidence interval \(\psi\) \(\hat{\psi} \pm z_{1 - \alpha/2} \, \hat{s}(\hat{\psi})\). Exponentiating end points, \(\hat{\psi}_l\) \(\hat{\psi}_u\), gives interval \(\{\exp(\hat{\psi}_l), \exp(\hat{\psi}_u)\}\) \(\theta\). (cell zero, 0.5 first added every cell, vcd::fourfold().) pooled Berkeley data, \(\hat{\psi} = 0.610\) \(\hat{s} = 0.0639\), 95% interval odds ratio runs 1.624 2.087. 2. table end interval. limit turned \(2 \times 2\) table odds ratio. margins equated, table symmetric form \[ \begin{bmatrix} p & 1 - p \\ 1 - p & p \end{bmatrix} , \] whose odds ratio \(\theta = p^2 / (1 - p)^2\). Solving \(p\) gives \(p = \sqrt{\theta} / (1 + \sqrt{\theta})\). generally, table can found keeps observed row column totals required odds ratio; margins fixed, whole table follows single cell, root quadratic equation. 3. Draw tables like data. limiting table standardized way observed table (std, margin) drawn outlines quadrants. Berkeley data gives: Every row observed margins, 2691 male 1835 female applicants, 1755 admitted. balance among cells changes.

title: Fourfold displays for 2-by-2 tables — geom_fourfold
text: mapping Set aesthetic mappings created ggplot2::aes(). supplied inherit.aes = TRUE, combined plot's default mappings. data data display layer. NULL, default, data inherited plot. ... arguments passed ggplot2::layer(), typically fixed aesthetics colour linewidth. std Standardization method. "margins" fixes selected margins, "ind.max" divides panel largest cell, ".max" divides every panel largest cell complete layer. margin Integer vector selecting table margins std = "margins". Use c(1, 2) margins, 1 y margin, 2 x margin. conf_level Confidence level [0, 1). Set 0 suppress confidence rings. extended TRUE, use adjusted p-values emphasize association draw direction ticks. ticks Non-negative length association direction ticks geom's normalized panel coordinates. p_adjust_method Method passed stats::p.adjust() adjustment across panels. Defaults "holm", first value stats::p.adjust.methods. shape Shape cell sectors: "circle" (default, vcd::fourfold()) draws quarter-circles; "square" draws quarter-squares equal area. palette Character vector least six valid colours semantic order used fourfold_palette(). na.rm FALSE, default, missing observations removed warning. TRUE, removed silently. show.legend Logical indicating whether layer included legends. default FALSE semantic fills mapped aesthetic. inherit.aes FALSE, override rather combine plot's default aesthetic mappings.

text: Map two-level horizontal variable x, two-level vertical variable y, cell frequencies weight. weight omitted, row counts one observation. first x level drawn left second right; first y level drawn top second bottom. Set factor levels explicitly order matters. One panel must contain exactly one 2--2 table. Use ggplot2::facet_grid() ggplot2::facet_wrap() display stratified tables. Duplicate x/y combinations within panel summed missing cells completed zero counts. Odds ratios, Wald confidence intervals, extended-display p-values match calculations vcd::fourfold(). observed cell zero, 0.5 added four cells inference. P-values adjusted across panels layer. Confidence intervals adjusted. shape = "square", cell drawn quarter-square area corresponding quarter-circle (side \(r\sqrt{\pi}/2\) radius \(r\)), two shapes display table identical areas. Confidence rings become nested square outlines. Cell counts stay inside frame corners unless square, confidence outline, direction tick panel layer reach , always case std = "ind.max"; counts every panel placed just outside frame corners. six semantic fill colours supplied palette; mapped ggplot2 fill scale. Typography layout defaults controlled theme_fourfold().
